facts.text: Linwood grew around the 1837 conversion of a gristmill into Linwood Mills, becoming one of Delaware Valley's largest cotton and woolen factories.
The Philadelphia, Wilmington & Baltimore Railroad reached Linwood in 1838, and a local station by the 1870s spurred trade in produce and small‑scale growth.
Holy Saviour Church, founded in 1914, quickly became a social hub for the riverfront industrial neighborhood of Linwood.
John Fisher School opened in September 1917 and ranks among Pennsylvania's top 20% of private schools.
Linwood's name originated from Linwood Seminary, a girls' school founded around 1800 by the Misses Emanuel, highlighting early educational focus.
The area that is now Linwood was part of Lower Chichester Township, settled by Europeans in 1679 and incorporated in 1682 within Chester County.
